title: Andrew Tate Behind Bars. This Time He's Cooked.
dek: He sold a generation of boys the idea that he was untouchable. Now he's in a federal cell in Miami, losing fights and money, with three countries lined up to put him on trial.
body: For a few years Andrew Tate was the loudest man on every teenage boy's phone. Supercars, cigars, a 'Matrix' he said only he could see past, and a $49.99-a-month online school promising to make you rich and feared. He told his followers he was untouchable. Tonight he is sitting in a federal detention center in Miami, waiting to find out whether the United States hands him to Britain.

Nothing has been proven in court. Tate and his brother Tristan deny every allegation, and no court anywhere has convicted them of anything. But the empire is coming apart in public, one hearing at a time.
## How it started to crack

The first crack came in Romania. In April 2022, police raided the brothers' compound outside Bucharest after a tip passed along by the U.S. embassy. In December 2022 both brothers were arrested on suspicion of human trafficking and forming an organized crime group, and spent months in jail and then house arrest. In June 2023 prosecutors indicted them for rape, trafficking and running a criminal group. Authorities seized cars, property and Bitcoin, including a fleet of supercars.

Then Britain. In 2024 a London court issued an arrest warrant, and in May 2025 the Crown Prosecution Service authorized 21 charges, including rape and human trafficking. Four women separately sued Andrew in London's High Court, alleging abuse that he denies. In December 2024 a British court let Devon and Cornwall Police seize roughly £2.5 million in unpaid tax.
## The escape that wasn't

In February 2025 the brothers flew out of Romania on a private jet and landed in Florida, cheered on by supporters who called it a victory. It wasn't. Within weeks, Florida's attorney general opened a criminal investigation. In April 2026 a Romanian court lifted the last of their travel restrictions, but prosecutors there kept digging.

On July 18, 2026, U.S. Marshals arrested both brothers in Miami on a sealed British warrant. The CPS added 38 new charges, bringing the total to 59. Andrew alone now faces counts including seven more of rape, three of facilitating sex trafficking, three of assault and 19 involving indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. The CPS says there are seven alleged victims and the alleged offenses span 2010 to 2017.
> A political hit. (Joseph McBride, the Tates' lawyer, on the July arrests)
## Locked up and losing

On September 9, Magistrate Judge Lauren Louis denied bail, finding the brothers hadn't shown they weren't a danger to the community. Their lawyer's emergency petition calling the detention unconstitutional hasn't sprung them. On October 9 the judge set separate final extradition hearings: November 19 for Andrew, November 20 for Tristan, refusing to merge them because of 'material differences' in the allegations. Even if a judge rules for extradition, the final call belongs to the State Department. The White House has said it won't step in.

Romania isn't done either. In September 2026 prosecutors there filed a new indictment accusing Andrew of trafficking minors, sex with a minor, money laundering and witness tampering, with Tristan accused of complicity.

## The money and the myth

Tate built his brand on being rich. The paper trail is thinner. He has claimed to be a billionaire; Romanian prosecutors documented about $12.3 million in assets in 2023, much of it now frozen. His Hustler's University course peaked at around 221,000 paying members in 2022, by its own unaudited count, before he was kicked off most major platforms. His DADDY memecoin collapsed more than 90 percent from its peak.

And the tough-guy act took a hit no lawyer can fix. On December 20, 2025, in Dubai, Tate stepped into a boxing ring with former NFL player Chase DeMoor and lost a majority decision over six rounds. The internet turned the fight into a meme within the hour, and MMA reporter Ariel Helwani called it the year's biggest 'fraud check.'
## The Report's take

Tate's real product was never crypto or courses. It was certainty: a man who said he had it all figured out and dared anyone to touch him. Courts in three countries are now touching him. Whatever the verdicts turn out to be, the myth of the untouchable alpha is already dead. The boys who bought it deserve to watch how it ends.
Tate and his brother deny all charges and allegations. Every count described here is an accusation, not a finding of guilt.
